questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: CERN. Mountains. I like mountains.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: There was an intro session with most of the information I needed so I would say quite easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Lots of help from their contact Arnaud and ESN.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Really easy via Airbnb but expensive. A bit harder to find the good offers at first cause it seemed like the good sites/platform where in French but after establishing a network down here it became way easier to find accommodation.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: That it works well I guess.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The housing market i generally tough here so it's hard to give it a good score but that's just the reality of Geneva I guess. The last couple of months I lived in Cité Universitaire instead of France. I lived in building A so I can't speak for the other buildings but to me there were 3 major problems living here. 1: No AC. 2: Noise from construction work. 3: Kitchens having no utensils and being more dirty than anything I have ever seen. Especially 1 and 2 together made it practically impossible to get more than 4-5 hours of sleep every single night so I would recommend finding anything else.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There was no central way to register for courses and no single email/person/institution to contact. We figured it out but it was a mess imo especially because of the fact that I had courses at 2 different faculties.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Sending emails back and fourth between different people and filling out forms. Lots of emails.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Basically everyone I reached out to was friendly and helpful so I wasn't worried about finding out how to register for courses. It just required a lot of emails.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I would say 10/10 when it comes to the host institution but 5/10 when it comes to the sending institution. My main problem being that it was really difficult to get pre-approval for the courses I actually wanted to take

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Begin asking around early and be prepared to write a lot of emails.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Physics courses were really good but some of the computer science courses weren't as fleshed out or relevant to me. This was mainly a problem because I couldn't get the pre-approval I had hoped for though.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Generally speaking the level of the courses themselves felt lower but exams were harder. The curriculum was never conceptually hard to grasp but generally had to be memorised to a higher degree than what I'm used to back in Copenhagen. Higher bar to pass when exams are oral without preparation time.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching itself was not that different imo but the evaluation method was. More oral exams here which I generally like but they had no preparation time so I feel like the focus became more about memorising curriculum than being able to look up and use tools whenever you need them.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Physics Applications of AI
Scientific Computing and Software Design for Physicists
Information Retrieval
Data Mining
Crowdsourcing and AI
Selected Chapters
Computational Imaging

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Scientific Computing and Software Design for Physicists might very well have been the best course I have ever had. Just 10/10 in any way you can imagine.

Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Almost anything you can think of. 10/10.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Nothing in particular cause it all depends on what you like.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Whatever they like.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy. Geneva is so international that it feels like there isn't a certain culture you have to get into at all. Everyone has their own individual background and that works really well.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Can't think of any.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I don't know honestly.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Bring money. Find a place with AC and a kitchen (not Cité Universitaire building A). Make friends.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not particularly.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Establishing a social network in a different country.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Trying to sleep without AC.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
